messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: DIF/DTF and multidimensional IRT
parts:
On Thu, Mar 15, 2018 at 11:49 AM, Dirk Pelt <dirkp...@gmail.com> wrote:
Actually, thinking about it a bit more, if simple structure is assumed, can we then proceed with "normal" DIF analyses? Since the probability of endorsing an item only depends on one trait only.

Generally, yes. If the latent traits are assumed to be uncorrelated then subsetting the unidimensional items in isolation is exactly the same as performing DIF on a model with simple structure. And, even if the traits were correlated, you'd likely do as well anyway, and the Type I errors would remain optimally (potentially, there may be slightly less power, depending on the degree of correlation, but in general I wouldn't see this as a problem). HTH.

Phil

I can't find much on this, how simple structure affects DIF analyses.

Any help would be appreciated! Best, Dirk
